summary: A Livemint article dated 20 Feb 2023 explains NEOM, Saudi Arabia's futuristic megacity project on the Red Sea coast, described as a city without roads and cars. It covers the project's scale, the Crown Prince's role, the planned districts including THE LINE, clean energy and green hydrogen plans, population targets, and transport and tourism plans. The surrounding page is mostly site navigation, stock tickers and unrelated headlines, which were ignored.
one_line: Livemint explainer on NEOM, Saudi Arabia's planned 26,500 sq km Red Sea megacity with no roads or cars, powered by renewables.
key_facts: NEOM is a combination of the Greek word NEO (new) and M, the first letter of the Arab word Mustakbal (the Future) and of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
Nearly 20% of infrastructure works at NEOM, Saudi Arabia's $500 billion futuristic city, are completed according to the agency's report.
The brainchild of NEOM is Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, also known as MBS.
The megacity project will spread across 26,500 sq. kilometres on the Red Sea coast, an area larger than Kuwait or Israel.
NEOM will be split into 10 different regions, including a floating port, a ski resort in the Sarwat Mountains, and a mirrored city.
By 2026 NEOM is expected to house some 450,000 people, rising to 1.5 to 2 million people by 2030.
Eventually THE LINE will be home to nine million residents and will be built with a footprint of just 34 sq km.
THE LINE will be 100 m tall, 200 metres wide and 170 km long, with a mirror glass facade.
All energy in NEOM will come 100% from renewable energy sources, the sun and the wind, plus hydrogen-based power generation.
NEOM will feature the world's largest green hydrogen production plant.
NEOM aims to become 'the world's most food self-sufficient city' using vertical farming and greenhouses, in a country that currently imports about 80 percent of its food.
Saudi Arabia will offer direct flights from NEOM to London and Dubai, and the city will use a next-generation transport mode called a Volocopter.
Trojena has been awarded the Asian Winter Games in 2029 and lies about 50 kilometres from the Gulf of Aqaba coast in the Sarwat Mountains, at elevations of 1,500-2,600 metres.
Oxagon will be a gateway for clean industries, Sindalah a luxury island destination for tourism, and Trojena a mountain destination.
